name: Sayyid dynasty
alt: Sayyid Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate

predecessors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
predecessors.text: Delhi and its surroundings, taken from Daulat Khan Lodi, who held the city after the last Tughlaqs

successors.name: Lodi dynasty
successors.text: Delhi, the Sayyid realm handed to Bahlul Lodi by Alam Shah's abdication

ledger.x: 28 May 1414: Khizr Khan takes Delhi and founds the Sayyid dynasty.
28 May 1414: the Sayyids hold Delhi as Timurid vassals.
1418: 'Har Singh rebelled again but was decisively defeated by Taj-ul-Mulk.'
1421: the allegiance is dropped, a bridge.
April 1451 at the latest: Gwalior is no longer the Sayyids', a bridge.
19/20 April 1451: Alam Shah abdicates to Bahlul Lodi.

wars.name: Katehar campaigns
wars.outcome: Har Singh surrendered and agreed to pay tribute in 1414; he rebelled again and was decisively defeated by Taj-ul-Mulk in 1418.

wars.name: Annexation of Bayana and Gwalior
wars.outcome: Taj-ul-Mulk's army was sent in July 1416 and annexed both regions.

wars.name: Sayyid-Malwa war
wars.outcome: Mubarak Shah defeated 'the advancing Hoshang Shah Ghori, the ruler of the Malwa Sultanate' and forced him to pay tribute (page gives the span 1421-1434).

wars.name: Sharqi invasion of Delhi
wars.outcome: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi 'annexed large parts of the Delhi Sultanate and besieged Delhi'; Muhammad Shah 'sought for peace and offered a matrimonial alliance', his daughter Bibi Raji marrying Ibrahim's son Mahmud Khan.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is recorded on the pages opened; the realm is Delhi, the Doab towns and fiefs, and its limits are approximate.
